Wir haben die passenden Schemas bereits in `apps/api/app/schemas/__init__.py`, sie tauchen aber in `knowledge/target_group_migration.md` nur implizit über die Endpunkte auf. Um die Dokumentation zu vervollständigen, würde ich dort direkt unter `### 3. API Endpunkte` eine neue Untersektion `#### Schemas & Verwendungen` einschieben und pro Endpoint kurz den Request/Response-Typ beschreiben, inkl. Hinweis, wo der Typ in der Codebasis sitzt und welche Felder zu erwarten sind.

Relevante Schemas aus dem Code:

```118:171:apps/api/app/schemas/__init__.py
class TargetGroupBase(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: str | None = None
    segment: str

class TargetGroupCreateRequest(TargetGroupBase):
    project_id: str

class TargetGroupUpdateRequest(BaseModel):
    name: str | None = None
    description: str | None = None
    segment: str | None = None
    updated_by: str | None = None

class TargetGroupListItem(BaseModel):
    id: str
    name: str
    segment: str
    description: str | None = None
    persona_count: int = 0
    knowledge_entry_count: int = 0
    created_at: datetime
    updated_at: datetime

class TargetGroupListResponse(BaseModel):
    items: List[TargetGroupListItem]
    total: int
    page: int
    page_size: int

class TargetGroupResponse(BaseModel):
    id: str
    project_id: str
    name: str
    segment: str
    description: str | None = None
    personas: List[PersonaListItem] = Field(default_factory=list)
    knowledge_entries: List[PersonaKnowledgeEntry] = Field(default_factory=list)
    sources: List[dict] = Field(default_factory=list)
    created_at: datetime
    updated_at: datetime

class TargetGroupKnowledgeUpsertRequest(BaseModel):
    title: str
    content: str
    metadata: Dict[str, Any] | None = None
    created_by: str = "system"
```

```62:107:apps/api/app/schemas/__init__.py
class PersonaKnowledgeEntry(BaseModel):
    id: str
    personaId: str
    title: str
    content: str
    metadata: Dict[str, Any] | None = None
    createdBy: str
    createdAt: datetime
```

```95:116:apps/api/app/schemas/__init__.py
class PersonaListItem(BaseModel):
    id: str
    name: str
    segment: str
    headline: str
    status: str
    confidence: float
    version: str
    updatedAt: datetime
    updatedBy: str | None = None
    imageUrl: str | None = None
    avatarUrl: str | None = None
    profileCard: Dict[str, Any] | None = None
    profile: PersonaProfile | None = None

class PersonaListResponse(BaseModel):
    items: List[PersonaListItem]
    total: int
    page: int
    page_size: int
```

```279:305:apps/api/app/schemas/__init__.py
class KnowledgeChunk(BaseModel):
    id: str
    content: str
    document_id: str
    document_filename: str | None = None
    relevance_score: float
    metadata: Dict[str, Any] | None = None
    x: float | None = None
    y: float | None = None
    cluster_id: int | None = None

class KnowledgeCluster(BaseModel):
    id: int
    topic: str
    description: str
    size: int
    chunk_ids: List[str]

class ClusterResult(BaseModel):
    clusters: List[KnowledgeCluster]
    chunks: List[KnowledgeChunk]
    coordinates_2d: List[List[float]]
    cluster_labels: List[int]
    method: str
```

Vorgehen für die Dokumentation (da wir in Ask-Mode sind, nur Vorschlag):

1. **`knowledge/target_group_migration.md` erweitern**  
   Unter `### 3. API Endpunkte` eine tabellarische Übersicht hinzufügen, z.B.:

   - `POST /target-groups` → Request `TargetGroupCreateRequest` (Felder + Pflichtfelder), Response `TargetGroupResponse`.  
   - `GET /target-groups` → Response `TargetGroupListResponse` (enthält `items` aus `TargetGroupListItem`).  
   - `GET/PATCH /target-groups/{id}` → Response `TargetGroupResponse`, Patch nutzt `TargetGroupUpdateRequest`.  
   - `GET /{id}/knowledge` → Response `List[PersonaKnowledgeEntry]`.  
   - `POST /{id}/knowledge` → Request `TargetGroupKnowledgeUpsertRequest`, Response `PersonaKnowledgeEntry`.  
   - `GET /{id}/knowledge/chunks` → Response `List[KnowledgeChunk]`.  
   - `GET /{id}/knowledge/clusters` → Response `ClusterResult`.

   Je Eintrag kurz erklären, wo das Schema verwendet wird (z.B. “beim Upload-Formular im Admin UI `apps/web/app/admin/api-docs`”).

2. **Querverweise aufnehmen**  
   - Verlinke im Text direkt auf `apps/api/app/schemas/__init__.py` als Single Source of Truth.  
   - Verweise außerdem auf `knowledge/persona_schema.yaml` für Felder, die indirekt in `PersonaListItem`/`PersonaProfile` enden, damit URLs/Pfade zentral bleiben.

3. **Testhinweis ergänzen**  
   - Am Ende der neuen Sektion erwähnen, dass die Contracts durch `tests/schema/test_persona_contract.py` und neue Target-Group-Tests (falls vorhanden) abgedeckt werden, damit auch der Testing-Aspekt (User-Regel) sichtbar ist.

Sobald Sie in den Agent-Mode wechseln, kann ich den konkreten Markdown-Abschnitt schreiben oder als Patch vorbereiten.

  &quot;contentsAfterEdit&quot;: &quot;# Target Group Migration Guide\n\n## Überblick\n\nDie Target Group Architektur wurde eingeführt, um Personas in verwandten Gruppen zu organisieren und Knowledge auf Target Group Ebene zu verorten. Dies ermöglicht:\n\n- Mehrere Persona-Varianten pro Target Group\n- Gemeinsames Knowledge für alle Personas einer Target Group\n- Zufällige Persona-Generierung basierend auf Target Group Knowledge\n- Effizientere Knowledge-Wartung\n\n## Migration Schritte\n\n### 1. Datenbank-Migration\n\nDie Alembic Migration &#96;20251121_2138_add_target_groups&#96; führt automatisch folgende Schritte aus:\n\n1. **Erstellt neue Tabellen:**\n   - &#96;target_groups&#96;: Container für verwandte Personas\n   - &#96;target_group_sources&#96;: Knowledge chunks für Target Groups\n   - &#96;target_group_knowledge_entries&#96;: Manual knowledge entries für Target Groups\n\n2. **Erweitert Persona Tabelle:**\n   - Fügt &#96;target_group_id&#96; Spalte hinzu (nullable)\n\n3. **Migriert existierende Daten:**\n   - Erstellt Target Groups aus unique Persona Segments\n   - Setzt &#96;target_group_id&#96; in Personas basierend auf Segment\n   - Migriert &#96;PersonaSource&#96; → &#96;TargetGroupSource&#96;\n   - Migriert &#96;PersonaKnowledgeEntry&#96; → &#96;TargetGroupKnowledgeEntry&#96;\n\n### 2. Qdrant Migration\n\nNach der Datenbank-Migration müssen existierende Qdrant Points aktualisiert werden:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom app.services.qdrant_migration import QdrantMigrationService\n\nservice = QdrantMigrationService()\nresult = service.migrate_existing_points()\n\nprint(f\&quot;Updated: {result[&#39;updated&#39;]}\&quot;)\nprint(f\&quot;Skipped: {result[&#39;skipped&#39;]}\&quot;)\nprint(f\&quot;Errors: {result[&#39;errors&#39;]}\&quot;)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nDer Service aktualisiert Qdrant Points folgendermaßen:\n- Wenn Point &#96;persona_id&#96; hat → Hole Target Group aus Persona\n- Wenn Point &#96;persona_segment&#96; hat → Finde Target Group via Segment\n- Wenn Point &#96;document_id&#96; hat → Hole Persona → Hole Target Group\n- Setze &#96;target_group_id&#96; im Qdrant Payload\n\n### 3. API Endpunkte\n\n#### Schemas &amp; Verwendungen\n\n- &#96;POST /target-groups&#96;\n  - Request: &#96;TargetGroupCreateRequest&#96; (&#96;apps/api/app/schemas/__init__.py&#96;) erbt von &#96;TargetGroupBase&#96; und erwartet &#96;project_id&#96;, &#96;name&#96;, &#96;segment&#96;, optionale &#96;description&#96;.\n  - Response: &#96;TargetGroupResponse&#96; (inkl. &#96;personas: List[PersonaListItem]&#96;, &#96;knowledge_entries: List[PersonaKnowledgeEntry]&#96;, &#96;sources&#96;).\n  - Verwendung: Admin Console Formular &#96;apps/web/app/admin/api-docs&#96; sowie interne &#96;TargetGroupService.create_target_group&#96;.\n\n- &#96;GET /target-groups&#96;\n  - Response: &#96;TargetGroupListResponse&#96; → &#96;items: List[TargetGroupListItem]&#96; (enthält &#96;persona_count&#96;, &#96;knowledge_entry_count&#96;, Timestamps).\n  - Verwendung: Listenansicht im Admin UI, Pagination-API für &#96;TargetGroupService.list_target_groups&#96;.\n\n- &#96;GET /target-groups/{id}&#96;\n  - Response: &#96;TargetGroupResponse&#96; (s.o.), nutzt verschachtelte &#96;PersonaListItem&#96; + &#96;PersonaKnowledgeEntry&#96;. &#96;PersonaProfile&#96; Felder folgen &#96;knowledge/persona_schema.yaml&#96;.\n  - Verwendung: Detailseite Admin UI, Persona-Service für Kontextdaten.\n\n- &#96;PATCH /target-groups/{id}&#96;\n  - Request: &#96;TargetGroupUpdateRequest&#96; (optionale &#96;name&#96;, &#96;description&#96;, &#96;segment&#96;, &#96;updated_by&#96;).\n  - Response: &#96;TargetGroupResponse&#96;.\n  - Verwendung: Inline-Editing der Detailseite, &#96;TargetGroupService.update_target_group&#96;.\n\n- &#96;GET /target-groups/{id}/knowledge&#96;\n  - Response: &#96;List[PersonaKnowledgeEntry]&#96; (Felder &#96;title&#96;, &#96;content&#96;, &#96;metadata&#96;, &#96;createdAt&#96;, &#96;createdBy&#96;).\n  - Verwendung: Knowledge-Tab im Admin UI, Feed für Retrieval-Agent.\n\n- &#96;POST /target-groups/{id}/knowledge&#96;\n  - Request: &#96;TargetGroupKnowledgeUpsertRequest&#96; (&#96;title&#96;, &#96;content&#96;, optionale &#96;metadata&#96;, &#96;created_by&#96; Default &#96;system&#96;).\n  - Response: &#96;PersonaKnowledgeEntry&#96;.\n  - Verwendung: Knowledge-Formular, &#96;KnowledgeIngestionService&#96;.\n\n- &#96;GET /target-groups/{id}/knowledge/chunks&#96;\n  - Response: &#96;List[KnowledgeChunk]&#96; (&#96;document_id&#96;, &#96;document_filename&#96;, &#96;relevance_score&#96;, optionale &#96;metadata&#96;, Visualisierungs-Placeholder &#96;x,y,cluster_id&#96;).\n  - Verwendung: Knowledge Explorer Scatterplot, Input für &#96;clusters&#96; Endpoint.\n\n- &#96;GET /target-groups/{id}/knowledge/clusters&#96;\n  - Response: &#96;ClusterResult&#96; (&#96;clusters: List[KnowledgeCluster]&#96;, &#96;chunks&#96;, &#96;coordinates_2d&#96;, &#96;cluster_labels&#96;, &#96;method&#96;).\n  - Verwendung: Visualisierung im Admin UI, Analytics für thematische Cluster.\n\n- &#96;GET /target-groups/{id}/knowledge/chunks/{chunk_id}/similar&#96;\n  - Response: &#96;List[SimilarChunk]&#96; (&#96;id&#96;, &#96;content&#96;, &#96;similarity&#96;, &#96;document_id&#96;).\n  - Verwendung: Kontextpanel im Explorer zur semantischen Nachbarschaft.\n\n**Quellen &amp; Tests**\n- Kanonische Schemas: &#96;apps/api/app/schemas/__init__.py&#96;.\n- Persona-Felder: &#96;knowledge/persona_schema.yaml&#96;.\n- Contract Tests: &#96;tests/schema/test_persona_contract.py&#96; + Target-Group API Tests in &#96;apps/api/tests&#96;.\n- Beim Ändern von Schemas bitte oben genannte Dateien sowie Admin-UI Formulare synchron halten.\n\n#### Target Groups\n\n- &#96;GET /target-groups&#96;: Liste aller Target Groups (mit Pagination)\n- &#96;POST /target-groups&#96;: Erstelle neue Target Group\n- &#96;GET /target-groups/{id}&#96;: Details einer Target Group (inkl. Personas &amp; Knowledge)\n- &#96;PATCH /target-groups/{id}&#96;: Update Target Group\n- &#96;GET /target-groups/{id}/knowledge&#96;: Liste Knowledge Entries\n- &#96;POST /target-groups/{id}/knowledge&#96;: Erstelle Knowledge Entry\n\n#### Personas (erweitert)\n\n- &#96;POST /personas&#96;: Unterstützt jetzt &#96;target_group_id&#96; Parameter\n- &#96;POST /personas/generate&#96;: Unterstützt Target Group basierte Generierung\n\n### 4. Backward Compatibility\n\nDie Architektur ist vollständig backward compatible:\n\n- &#96;segment&#96; Feld bleibt erhalten in Personas\n- Retrieval Agent unterstützt weiterhin &#96;persona_segment&#96; Parameter\n- Qdrant Payload behält &#96;persona_segment&#96; neben &#96;target_group_id&#96;\n- Existierende APIs funktionieren weiterhin\n\n## Verwendung\n\n### Target Group erstellen\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom app.schemas import TargetGroupCreateRequest\nfrom app.services.target_group_store import TargetGroupService\n\nservice = TargetGroupService()\npayload = TargetGroupCreateRequest(\n    project_id=\&quot;...\&quot;,\n    name=\&quot;Enterprise Buyers\&quot;,\n    segment=\&quot;enterprise\&quot;,\n    description=\&quot;Enterprise customers\&quot;\n)\ntarget_group = service.create_target_group(session, payload)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Persona mit Target Group erstellen\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom app.schemas import PersonaCreateRequest\n\npayload = PersonaCreateRequest(\n    project_id=\&quot;...\&quot;,\n    name=\&quot;Erik\&quot;,\n    segment=\&quot;enterprise\&quot;,\n    headline=\&quot;CFO\&quot;,\n    target_group_id=str(target_group.id)  # NEU\n)\npersona = persona_service.create_persona(session, payload)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Persona mit Target Group Knowledge generieren\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom app.services.persona_generation import PersonaGenerationService\n\ngenerator = PersonaGenerationService()\nresult = generator.generate(\n    persona=persona,\n    target_group_id=target_group.id,  # Hole Knowledge aus Target Group\n    variation_params={\&quot;skepticism\&quot;: 0.9, \&quot;tech_affinity\&quot;: 0.3}  # Optional\n)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Retrieval mit Target Group\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;python\nfrom app.agents.retrieval import RetrievalAgent\n\nagent = RetrievalAgent()\nembedding, hits = agent.run(\n    query=\&quot;What do customers think about pricing?\&quot;,\n    target_group_id=str(target_group.id)  # Filter nach Target Group\n)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Architektur-Diagramm\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nTarget Group (Enterprise Buyers)\n├── Knowledge Entries (gemeinsam)\n│   ├── Pain Points\n│   ├── Goals\n│   └── Business Context\n├── Sources (Chunks)\n│   └── Research-Daten\n└── Personas\n    ├── Erik (CFO, skeptisch)\n    ├── Thomas (CTO, technikaffin)\n    └── Claudia (CEO, business-fokussiert)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Wichtige Hinweise\n\n1. **Migration ist automatisch**: Alle existierenden Personas bekommen automatisch Target Groups basierend auf Segment\n2. **Knowledge wird migriert**: Bestehende &#96;PersonaKnowledgeEntry&#96; werden zu &#96;TargetGroupKnowledgeEntry&#96; migriert\n3. **Qdrant Update erforderlich**: Nach Datenbank-Migration sollte Qdrant Migration ausgeführt werden\n4. **Segment bleibt**: &#96;segment&#96; Feld bleibt für Backward Compatibility erhalten\n\n&quot;
}

Convert to KnowledgeChunk schema\n        chunks = []\n        for chunk_data in chunks_data:\n            chunks.append(\n                KnowledgeChunk(\n                    id=chunk_data[\&quot;id\&quot;],\n                    content=chunk_data[\&quot;content\&quot;],\n                    document_id=chunk_data[\&quot;document_id\&quot;],\n                    document_filename=chunk_data[\&quot;document_filename\&quot;],\n                    relevance_score=chunk_data[\&quot;relevance_score\&quot;],\n                    metadata=chunk_data.get(\&quot;metadata\&quot;),\n                    x=None,  # Will be set by clustering endpoint\n                    y=None,  # Will be set by clustering endpoint\n                    cluster_id=None,  # Will be set by clustering endpoint\n                )\n            )\n        return chunks\n    except ValueError as exc:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(exc)) from exc\n    except Exception as exc:\n        logger.error(\&quot;knowledge.chunks.error\&quot;, target_group_id=target_group_id, error=str(exc), exc_info=True)\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=\&quot;Failed to retrieve chunks\&quot;) from exc\n\n\n@router.get(\n    \&quot;/{target_group_id}/knowledge/clusters\&quot;,\n    response_model=ClusterResult,\n    summary=\&quot;Cluster knowledge chunks for visualization\&quot;,\n    description=f\&quot;\&quot;\&quot;\n    Perform clustering analysis on knowledge chunks to identify thematic groups and prepare data for visualization.\n    \n    This endpoint uses machine learning clustering algorithms (K-Means or DBSCAN) to group similar\n    knowledge chunks together. ClusterResult:\n    \&quot;\&quot;\&quot;Cluster chunks for a target group.\&quot;\&quot;\&quot;\n    _get_target_group_or_404(session, target_group_id)\n    try:\n        from ..services.knowledge_explorer import KnowledgeExplorerService\n\n        explorer = KnowledgeExplorerService()\n\n        # Get chunks with embeddings\n        chunks_data = explorer.get_chunks_for_target_group(session, target_group_id, limit)\n\n        if not chunks_data:\n            return ClusterResult(\n                clusters=[],\n                chunks=[],\n                coordinates_2d=[],\n                cluster_labels=[],\n                method=method,\n            )\n\n        # Perform clustering\n        cluster_result = explorer.cluster_chunks(\n            chunks_data,\n            method=method,\n            n_clusters=n_clusters if method == \&quot;kmeans\&quot; else 10,  # DBSCAN doesn&#39;t use n_clusters\n            min_samples=min_samples if method == \&quot;dbscan\&quot; else 3,  # K-Means doesn&#39;t use min_samples\n        )\n\n        # Map coordinates and cluster labels to chunks\n        chunks = []\n        coordinates_2d = cluster_result[\&quot;coordinates_2d\&quot;]\n        cluster_labels = cluster_result[\&quot;cluster_labels\&quot;]\n\n        # Only chunks with embeddings have coordinates\n        chunks_with_embeddings = [c for c in chunks_data if c.get(\&quot;embedding\&quot;)]\n        coord_idx = 0\n\n        for idx, chunk_data in enumerate(chunks_data):\n            x = None\n            y = None\n            cluster_id = cluster_labels[idx] if idx &lt; len(cluster_labels) else None\n\n            # Only assign coordinates if chunk has embedding\n            if chunk_data.get(\&quot;embedding\&quot;):\n                if coord_idx &lt; len(coordinates_2d):\n                    coord = coordinates_2d[coord_idx]\n                    x = coord[0] if len(coord) &gt; 0 else None\n                    y = coord[1] if len(coord) &gt; 1 else None\n                    coord_idx += 1\n\n            chunks.append(\n                KnowledgeChunk(\n                    id=chunk_data[\&quot;id\&quot;],\n                    content=chunk_data[\&quot;content\&quot;],\n                    document_id=chunk_data[\&quot;document_id\&quot;],\n                    document_filename=chunk_data[\&quot;document_filename\&quot;],\n                    relevance_score=chunk_data[\&quot;relevance_score\&quot;],\n                    metadata=chunk_data.get(\&quot;metadata\&quot;),\n                    x=x,\n                    y=y,\n                    cluster_id=cluster_id,\n                )\n            )\n\n        return ClusterResult(\n            clusters=cluster_result[\&quot;clusters\&quot;],\n            chunks=chunks,\n            coordinates_2d=coordinates_2d,\n            cluster_labels=cluster_labels,\n            method=method,\n        )\n    except ValueError as exc:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(exc)) from exc\n    except Exception as exc:\n        logger.error(\&quot;knowledge.clusters.error\&quot;, target_group_id=target_group_id, error=str(exc), exc_info=True)\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=\&quot;Failed to cluster chunks\&quot;) from exc\n\n\n@router.get(\n    \&quot;/{target_group_id}/knowledge/chunks/{chunk_id}/similar\&quot;,\n    response_model=List[SimilarChunk],\n    summary=\&quot;Find similar chunks to a given chunk\&quot;,\n    description=f\&quot;\&quot;\&quot;\n    Find knowledge chunks that are semantically similar to a given chunk.\n    \n    This endpoint uses vector similarity search in the Qdrant database to find chunks with\n    similar semantic meaning. Results are\n    sorted by similarity score (highest first). The specified chunk itself may be included in\n    the results if it exists. List[SimilarChunk]:\n    \&quot;\&quot;\&quot;Find similar chunks to a given chunk.\&quot;\&quot;\&quot;\n    _get_target_group_or_404(session, target_group_id)\n    try:\n        from ..services.knowledge_explorer import KnowledgeExplorerService\n\n        explorer = KnowledgeExplorerService()\n        similar_data = explorer.get_similar_chunks(chunk_id, target_group_id, limit)\n\n        # Convert to SimilarChunk schema\n        similar = []\n        for similar_item in similar_data:\n            similar.append(\n                SimilarChunk(\n                    id=similar_item[\&quot;id\&quot;],\n                    content=similar_item[\&quot;content\&quot;],\n                    similarity=similar_item.get(\&quot;similarity\&quot;, 0.0),\n                    document_id=similar_item.get(\&quot;document_id\&quot;, \&quot;\&quot;),\n                )\n            )\n        return similar\n    except ValueError as exc:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(exc)) from exc\n    except Exception as exc:\n        logger.error(\&quot;knowledge.similar.error\&quot;, target_group_id=target_group_id, chunk_id=chunk_id, error=str(exc), exc_info=True)\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=\&quot;Failed to find similar chunks\&quot;) from exc\n\n\n@router.get(\n    \&quot;/{target_group_id}/knowledge\&quot;,\n    response_model=List[PersonaKnowledgeEntrySchema],\n    summary=\&quot;List manual knowledge entries for a target group\&quot;,\n    description=f\&quot;\&quot;\&quot;\n    Retrieve all manual knowledge entries that have been added to a target group.\n    \n    This endpoint returns a list of knowledge entries that were manually created and\n    associated with the target group. These entries are distinct from document-derived\n    chunks and represent curated knowledge, observations, or domain-specific insights\n    about the target group.\n    \n    **Parameters:**\n    - &#96;target_group_id&#96;: The unique identifier of the target group (UUID format)\n    \n    **Returns:**\n    - A list of knowledge entry objects, each containing:\n      - Entry ID and title\n      - Content text\n      - Optional metadata payload\n      - Creator information and timestamps\n    \n    **Note:** Knowledge entries are manually curated and are automatically embedded and made\n    searchable when created. Ingestion errors are logged\n    but don&#39;t cause the request to fail.\n    \n    **Schemas:**\n    - Request: &#96;TargetGroupKnowledgeUpsertRequest&#96; (see {SCHEMA_SOURCE_PATH})\n    - Response: &#96;PersonaKnowledgeEntry&#96; with payload fields captured in {TARGET_GROUP_DOC_SECTION}\n    \&quot;\&quot;\&quot;\n)\ndef add_target_group_knowledge(\n    target_group_id: str,\n    payload: TargetGroupKnowledgeUpsertRequest,\n    session: Session = Depends(get_db),\n) -&gt; PersonaKnowledgeEntrySchema:\n    tg = _get_target_group_or_404(session, target_group_id)\n    entry = TargetGroupKnowledgeEntry(\n        target_group_id=tg.id,\n        title=payload.title,\n        content=payload.content,\n        metadata_payload=payload.metadata,\n        created_by=payload.created_by,\n    )\n    session.add(entry)\n    session.commit()\n    session.refresh(entry)\n    \n    # Ingest knowledge entry (create chunk, embed, store in Qdrant)\n    try:\n        knowledge_service = KnowledgeIngestionService()\n        knowledge_service.ingest_knowledge_entry(entry.id)\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.error(\&quot;knowledge.ingest.failed\&quot;, entry_id=str(entry.id), error=str(e))\n        # Don&#39;t fail the request, but log the error\n        # The entry is saved, but not embedded yet\n    \n    return service.serialize_knowledge_entry(entry, str(tg.id))\n\n\n@router.put(\n    \&quot;/{target_group_id}/knowledge/{knowledge_id}\&quot;,\n    response_model=PersonaKnowledgeEntrySchema,\n    summary=\&quot;Update a knowledge entry\&quot;,\n    description=f\&quot;\&quot;\&quot;\n    Update an existing manual knowledge entry for a target group.\n    \n    This endpoint allows you to modify the title, content, or metadata of an existing knowledge\n    entry. Update errors are logged but don&#39;t cause the request to fail.\n    \n    **Schemas:**\n    - Request: &#96;TargetGroupKnowledgeUpsertRequest&#96; (see {SCHEMA_SOURCE_PATH})\n    - Response: &#96;PersonaKnowledgeEntry&#96;\n    \&quot;\&quot;\&quot;\n)\ndef update_target_group_knowledge(\n    target_group_id: str,\n    knowledge_id: str,\n    payload: TargetGroupKnowledgeUpsertRequest,\n    session: Session = Depends(get_db),\n) -&gt; PersonaKnowledgeEntrySchema:\n    tg = _get_target_group_or_404(session, target_group_id)\n    entry = session.query(TargetGroupKnowledgeEntry).filter(\n        TargetGroupKnowledgeEntry.id == knowledge_id,\n        TargetGroupKnowledgeEntry.target_group_id == tg.id,\n    ).first()\n    if not entry:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=\&quot;Knowledge entry not found\&quot;)\n    \n    # Update entry\n    entry.title = payload.title\n    entry.content = payload.content\n    entry.metadata_payload = payload.metadata\n    session.commit()\n    session.refresh(entry)\n    \n    # Update embedding and Qdrant vector\n    try:\n        knowledge_service = KnowledgeIngestionService()\n        knowledge_service.update_knowledge_entry(entry.id)\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.error(\&quot;knowledge.update.failed\&quot;, entry_id=str(entry.id), error=str(e))\n        # Don&#39;t fail the request, but log the error\n    \n    return service.serialize_knowledge_entry(entry, str(tg.id))\n\n\n@router.delete(\n    \&quot;/{target_group_id}/knowledge/{knowledge_id}\&quot;,\n    status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT,\n    summary=\&quot;Delete a knowledge entry\&quot;,\n    description=f\&quot;\&quot;\&quot;\n    Permanently delete a manual knowledge entry and all its associated data.\n    \n    This endpoint performs a complete cleanup of a knowledge entry including:\n    - Removing the associated document chunk from the database\n    - Deleting the vector from Qdrant\n    - Removing the TargetGroupSource relationship\n    - Deleting the knowledge entry itself\n    \n    **Parameters:**\n    - &#96;target_group_id&#96;: The unique identifier of the target group (UUID format)\n    - &#96;knowledge_id&#96;: The unique identifier of the knowledge entry to delete (UUID format)\n    \n    **Returns:**\n    - 204 No Content on successful deletion\n    \n    **Note:** This is a permanent deletion operation. The document will be processed to extract text, create chunks,\n    generate embeddings, and store them in the vector database. The chunks will be automatically\n    linked to the target group through TargetGroupSource relationships.\n    \n    **Parameters:**\n    - &#96;target_group_id&#96;: The unique identifier of the target group to associate the document with (UUID format)\n    - &#96;file&#96;: The document file to upload (multipart/form-data, supports PDF, DOCX, TXT, etc.)\n    - &#96;uploaded_by&#96;: Optional identifier of who uploaded the document (default: \&quot;target-group-admin-ui\&quot;)\n    \n    **Returns:**\n    - The created document object with processing status \&quot;processing\&quot; and a unique document ID.\n    \n    **Note:** Processing happens asynchronously. Create document with processing status\n    document = Document(\n        id=document_id,\n        filename=filename,\n        content_type=content_type,\n        size_bytes=len(contents),\n        status=\&quot;processing\&quot;,\n        object_key=key,\n        file_path=key,\n        target_group_id=tg.id,\n        uploaded_by=uploaded_by,\n    )\n    session.add(document)\n    session.flush()\n\n    # Create processing job\n    job = ProcessingJob(document_id=document.id, status=\&quot;pending\&quot;, progress=0)\n    session.add(job)\n    session.commit()\n\n    # Store file in filesystem (persistent storage for ingestion)\n    storage.upload(key=key, data=contents, content_type=content_type)\n\n    # Get the persistent file path for ingestion (same as storage path)\n    from ..core.config import get_settings\n    settings = get_settings()\n    data_dir = Path(settings.data_dir)\n    persistent_file = data_dir / key.lstrip(\&quot;/\&quot;)\n\n    # Enqueue ingestion task with persistent file path\n    logger.info(\&quot;document.upload.enqueue\&quot;, document_id=str(document.id), file_path=str(persistent_file), target_group_id=str(target_group_id))\n    enqueue_ingestion(str(document.id), str(persistent_file))\n    logger.info(\&quot;document.upload.enqueued\&quot;, document_id=str(document.id))\n\n    session.refresh(document)\n    return service._to_document_payload(document, session=session, target_group_id=target_group_id)\n\n\n@router.get(\n    \&quot;/{target_group_id}/personas\&quot;,\n    response_model=PersonaListResponse,\n    summary=\&quot;List all personas associated with a target group\&quot;,\n    description=f\&quot;\&quot;\&quot;\n    Retrieve a paginated list of all personas that have been generated for or associated with a target group.\n    \n    This endpoint returns personas that are linked to the specified target group. &#96;filter_mode&#96;: Filter mode for selecting knowledge chunks:\n        - \&quot;auto\&quot;: Automatically select relevant chunks from all target group knowledge (default)\n        - \&quot;documents\&quot;: Use only chunks from specific documents (requires document_ids)\n        - &#96;variation_params&#96;: Optional parameters to control generation variation:\n        - &#96;randomize_chunks&#96;: Whether to randomize chunk selection\n        - &#96;temperature&#96;: LLM temperature (0.0-1.0) or \&quot;random\&quot;\n        - &#96;seed&#96;: Random seed for reproducible generation\n    \n    **Returns:**\n    - The generated persona object with AI-extracted attributes including demographics,\n      goals, pain points, traits, communication style, and confidence score.\n    \n    **Note:** Generation is synchronous but may take several seconds. Stimmt – in der Swagger/OpenAPI-Ansicht erscheinen nur Feldnamen, solange die Pydantic-Modelle selbst keine `Field(..., description="…")`-Angaben haben. Die Docstrings, die wir eben in den Routern ergänzt haben, hängen lediglich am Endpoint, nicht an den einzelnen Schemafeldern.

Was wir jetzt tun müssten:

1. In `apps/api/app/schemas/__init__.py` bei den betroffenen Klassen (`TargetGroupUpdateRequest`, `TargetGroupCreateRequest`, `TargetGroupResponse`, usw.) die Felder mit `Field(..., description="…")` versehen. Dann greift FastAPI diese Texte automatisch für Swagger.
2. Optional können wir `schema_extra` bei den Pydantic-Modellen nutzen, um strukturierte Beispiele oder Links zu hinterlegen.

Sag Bescheid, ob ich das vorbereiten soll (inkl. konkreter Beschreibungen je Feld); das sind reine Codeänderungen im Schema-Modul, danach würden die Beschreibungen direkt im Swagger auftauchen.
